speaker_role: current admissions dean (Dean Jobson, Harvard Law School), per host introduction
commercial_incentive: Host channel (Becoming LawyHer) runs a law-applicant community and edits statements; guest has none evident.
key_insights: Off-topic for undergraduate admissions: this is a law school interview about two required written statements, interviews and file review.
Overlap between the two statements is fine if each takes a different lens, one forward-looking and one reflective.
Cohesion across resume and essays helps only when authentic; over-engineered narratives can fall apart in interviews.
Applicants are not expected to be unique; readers want a strong academic fit and a good community member.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Guest says HLS interviews about 1,200-1,400 candidates a year and admits about 800 of them.
Guest says the most applications HLS ever received is just under 10,000.
Guest says the office uses randomized first and second readers, then group committee discussion, then faculty review.
notable_or_distinctive: Candid look at a multi-reader model and interview weight, but for graduate law admissions only.
reliability_notes: Law school content, not applicable to undergraduate admissions; captions clean but one figure is garbled.
